newsitem.title: INDONESIA: JAKARTA STOCKS SEEN SOFT AMID RUPIAH FALLS.
newsitem.headline: JAKARTA STOCKS SEEN SOFT AMID RUPIAH FALLS.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen soft on Wednesday, with a fresh plunge in the rupiah against the dollar seen further weakening sentiment, brokers said.

"Sentiment is likely to stay weak. We've got stories today which are mostly not encouraging. The rupiah continues falling while inflation is likely to be higher than expected," one broker with a state-owned brokerage said.
The Indonesian rupiah tumbled to a record low of 2,667/72 against the dollar at 0145 GMT on Wednesday from an opening of 2,643/50, dealers said.

Indonesia's Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) said the country's inflation rate this year was likely to be higher than the previous forecast of six percent if an ongoing drought lasts longer and the negative impacts could not be contained, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported.
On Tuesday, the Jakarta composite index was up 4.78 points, or 0.73 percent, to close at 662.95 points. The index had fallen to 647.17 points in the morning on the weak rupiah.
Brokers said sentiment had already been weak due to reports of possibly higher inflation this year if the ongoing draught in the country was prolonged.

Indonesia's Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) said the country's inflation rate this year was likely to be higher than the previos forecast of six percent if the drought continues and the negative impacts could not be contained, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported.
Among the losers were commodities-related companies Indofood, Budi Acid and Mayora.
